## Caption (Instagram)

## YouTube Shorts

**Title:** What actually happens when you post

**Description:**

```
A post isn't one photo, it's four things: copies, caches, screenshots, metadata. Deleting gets one back. The rest of this episode is three habits that let you keep posting without the uneasy feeling.

Sources:
- Content is commonly served to viewers from caches or content delivery networks rather than a single origin. (RFC 9111: HTTP Caching) https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111 checked 2026-10-28
- Caches keep local copies of responses to serve later requests faster. (RFC 9111: HTTP Caching) https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111 checked 2026-10-28
- A screenshot is produced by the viewer's device and is not something the platform can revoke. (Exif 3.0 specification (CIPA DC-008)) https://www.cipa.jp/std/documents/download_e.html?DC-008-Translation-2023-E checked 2026-10-28
- Image files can carry metadata such as capture time, device and location. (Exif 3.0 specification (CIPA DC-008)) https://www.cipa.jp/std/documents/download_e.html?DC-008-Translation-2023-E checked 2026-10-28
```
